transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood), Sofia (MarketBridge), Ethan (MarketBridge Eng), Nadia (MarketBridge PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the objectives — marketplace listing, reference arch, and joint solution patterns.
[00:12] Sofia: Hey yes hi, Sofia here. Thanks.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan on the line.
[00:18] Nadia: Nadia here.
[00:20] Priya: Priya from Redwood. Liam's on too.
[00:25] Jordan: Awesome, cool. Nadia I think you sent an agenda earlier, thanks for that. We'll go through the required artifacts for MarketBridge marketplace and then dive into the deployment options — hosted listing vs dedicated shared infra vs private VPC offering, and then the co-sell/marketing bits.

[01:05] Nadia: Yeah, our PM goal is to get a certified listing in the MarketBridge marketplace by early December. We also want a reference architecture for customers who will want private deployments behind their own VPCs.

[01:20] Priya: Great. Quick high-level: Redwood supports three main modes that map to what you described — hosted API listing (our hosted inference endpoints), Dedicated (reserved capacity we can tie to a partner SKU), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For the marketplace listing we'll need screenshots, an integration manifest, an icons/hero image, and a short technical blurb plus links to docs.

[01:46] Ethan: On the private side we're worried about network connectivity and billing. How does auth work if a customer buys via MarketBridge — do they get a marketplace invoice or does Redwood bill directly?

[02:02] Jordan: Good question. There are two patterns we've implemented: 1) marketplace-managed billing where MarketBridge handles the money and pushes a metered usage payload to Redwood via partner billing APIs, or 2) referral/lead flow where the customer signs up on the Redwood console and we invoice directly. We can do both but marketplace-managed needs an integration shim — a webhook and metering contract.

[02:28] Sofia: The marketplace prefers option 1 for a smoother buyer experience; they want the listing to be purchasable and have single invoice.

[02:35] Priya: That will require us to map Marketplace SKU to a Redwood plan and supply a metering endpoint. We also need to verify token exchange flows — we can provision short-lived keys for the deployed private runtime or offer a marketplace-linked account. We'll include our recommended flow in the reference doc.

[03:05] Liam: Also note there are SLA expectations for our Dedicated customers; if a customer picks a reserved capacity SKU via MarketBridge we need to ensure capacity mapping. That is, the marketplace SKU needs to map to a Redwood Dedicated capacity pool or a burstable plan that can be guaranteed.

[03:28] Nadia: For private deployments, our compliance team will require SOC2 and audit log evidence. Do you have a checklist we can include with the listing?

[03:36] Priya: Yes, we'll attach our security pack — SOC2, ISO certs, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit log export docs. We'll also add instructions for network egress rules and K8s Helm values for on-prem installs.

[03:55] Ethan: On the technical side, we need the reference arch to be prescriptive: e.g., how to route traffic from MarketBridge discovery to Redwood hosted API, and alternate flow for private. Can you show an example diagram?

[04:10] Priya: Sure, Liam has a diagram. (brief pause) Sorry, the export name is reference-arch-v1.png; link will be in the notes. High-level: marketplace listing -> buyer portal -> either (A) redirect to Redwood hosted endpoint with marketplace token OR (B) triggers a private deployment with a provisioned VPC peering and an API gateway in the customer's account. For (B) we use an agent or helm chart to deploy the runtime and configure KV cache helpers.

[04:45] Ethan: KV cache helpers? Can you expand — we're particularly concerned about cold-starts and latency for short chat sessions.

[04:51] Priya: Yeah so our runtime supports prefix caching/KV cache to reduce repeated token computation. For private deployments we recommend deploying a small warm pool and enabling local KV cache to minimize cold-start penalty. We'll include suggested instance types and quantization profiles — e.g., for 8-16 token median sequence length workload, q4_0 or q5_0 gives good cost/latency tradeoffs.

[05:20] Sofia: Are those quantization profiles documented anywhere? Our integrators will need specifics.

[05:23] Priya: Yes — we'll link to the optimize guide and include a table: recommended model variant, quantization, expected RPS per GPU, and latency estimates. We'll mark those as benchmarks though, since actual depends on prompt length.

[05:42] Jordan: Back to the marketplace listing — marketing wants a one-liner, 200-word description, 2 screenshots and a 60-second demo video. We usually provide a partner-friendly template screenshot with callouts for latency and cost-per-token metrics.

[06:00] Nadia: On the co-marketing side, we want a joint webinar and a blog post. Timeline wise, if listing goes live early December webinar in mid-Dec makes sense.

[06:12] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll propose dates.

[06:18] Ethan: Tech question — for private deployments how do we handle telemetry? We need logs to appear in MarketBridge's monitoring or at least be exportable.

[06:27] Priya: We can ship telemetry to an external endpoint using our tracing hooks; we support OTLP/Jaeger exports and can push metrics to a partner-managed Prometheus/Grafana. Audit logs can be streamed to S3 or a customer log sink. We'll include config snippets for that.

[06:50] Sofia: Is there any certification process on Redwood's side before we list? Some marketplaces require a security review and a test-run.

[06:58] Liam: We do recommend a short security checklist validation and a technical test-run where we demonstrate a provisioning flow and billing ping. For MarketBridge's marketplace-managed billing we'll run a simulated metered event in staging.

[07:14] Ethan: Good. On the integration API — what endpoints do you expose for partner metering and entitlement?

[07:20] Priya: We expose a partner-metering API that accepts JSON payloads with usage units and returns a 200/ack. We also have an entitlement endpoint that verifies tokens and maps to account quotas. We'll share the API proto in the doc. Note: naming in the doc may have some typos — earlier exports had Redwood-integra... sometimes the auto transcript mangles that — pardon.

[07:48] Jordan: (laughs) yeah transcripts love to mangle things.

[07:52] Nadia: For the pilot, we were thinking of 3 customers to try the private deployment flow — one small, one mid, one enterprise. We need a checklist of what we expect them to provide (VPC ranges, expected concurrency, preferred model choices).

[08:08] Priya: We'll produce a pilot readiness checklist: network, creds, traffic expectations, acceptance criteria (latency under X ms P95, cost per token within Y% of estimate), and rollback plan.

[08:25] Ethan: On the rollback plan — what happens if KV cache or model quantization regresses output quality? Do you have version pinning?

[08:33] Priya: Yes, model version pinning and rollout policies. We support canary deploys and A/B. Also Redwood Optimize will monitor prompt sets and alert if n-gram or eval metrics degrade beyond threshold. For pilot we'll recommend conservative quantization profiles.

[08:53] Sofia: Great. A couple of compliance items — we need KMS integration details and whether keys stay in customer account.

[09:00] Liam: For private installations keys can remain in the customer's KMS. For hosted we offer bring-your-own-key options using HSM-backed KMS; we'll outline the flows: cross-account grants or customer-managed HI... HSM. (brief pause) Sorry, HSM/KMS naming might be fuzzy on this aud.

[09:25] Nadia: That's fine, we just want clear instructions.

[09:28] Jordan: Let's talk timeline and deliverables. Priya will draft the reference architecture and helm chart link. Jordan will draft the marketplace listing copy and sample screenshots. We'll coordinate on the billing API contract and run a staging test.

[09:44] Ethan: Who will own the staging test?

[09:47] Jordan: Redwood SEs will run the staging test with MarketBridge engineers; we'll schedule a 90-minute session to execute the metering flow and a private deploy. Proposed date included in next steps.

[10:00] Nadia: OK. Also, do you have any example listings from other marketplaces we can use as a template?

[10:07] Priya: Yes — we'll share two examples — one hosted and one private.

[10:12] Sofia: Perfect. Anything else?

[10:15] Liam: One more technical note: if the marketplace needs to surface usage data to buyers in their portal we can provide a daily usage CSV export or a reporting API. We'll add that to the doc.

[10:28] Sofia: Excellent.

[10:30] Jordan: Alright let's recap the explicit next steps so it's clean in the notes...

[10:35] Jordan: Recap: Redwood to share marketplace listing draft, screenshots, and security pack by 2025-11-15; SE to upload reference architecture + helm chart by 2025-11-14; schedule staging integration test week of 2025-11-24; MarketBridge to confirm pilot customer list by 2025-11-19.

[11:00] Nadia: Sounds good to me.

[11:05] Ethan: Yep.

[11:07] Sofia: Thanks all.

[11:10] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and put the artifacts in the shared drive.

[11:15] (call ends)

Notes/links mentioned during call:
- reference-arch-v1.png (will be uploaded)
- helm chart: github.com/redwood-inference/marketbridge-helm (draft)
- partner metering API spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/partners/metering (draft)
- security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security/partner-pack.pdf
